title: ui tests: 51 type-level Equal pins on spec literal unions turn Type Check UI red when the spec adds a member
body:
Filing class: ③ CI brittleness (the type-level twin of #26238). Found by the #26238 sweep (PR #26272, os-dev-report https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/26238#issuecomment-6423766109), out of that card's runtime-test scope.

## What
51 `Equal<…>` type assertions in 31 spec-reading `ui/**` test files (at `df8aac41f`) pin a spec-owned literal union exactly, for example `ui/packages/plugin-chatbot/src/__tests__/spec-symbol-batch6.test.ts:251` (`PendingActionStatus`). When `@objectstack/spec` adds a member to one of those unions, **Type Check UI** goes red on every ui PR, although no ui behaviour changed. That is the same failure #26005 caused at runtime through the 47-key guards (#26218 / #26231), moved to the type checker.

## Why it needs a ruling per type
Unlike the runtime counts, some of these pins are deliberate. A union that ui renders exhaustively (a `switch` with a `never` default, or a label map typed `Record<Union, string>`) should break when the spec grows, because ui really is missing a case. Others only restate the spec. So each pin is one of:
- **exhaustive consumer:** keep exact `Equal`, and make sure the red points at the ui site that needs the new case;
- **restatement:** relax to `extends` (the members ui reads are still present) or delete it.

## Done when
- Every one of the 51 pins is listed with its verdict and a one-line reason.
- The restatements are relaxed, and the exhaustive ones are kept.
- A scratch spec member added to one restated union leaves Type Check UI green, and a member added to one exhaustive union turns it red at the consumer.

Related: #26238 (runtime sweep), #26092 (run ui checks on spec PRs).
